Placed fourth on the points table, the Kartik Sharma-led side finds itself chasing the front-runners, Mumbai, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu, all of whom have capitalised on at least one outright victory to surge ahead.With draws against Tamil Nadu and Railways yielding only three points apiece, securing dominant, bonus-point wins has become paramount if the side wishes to bridge the gap. The decision raised eyebrows given Lomror's proven track record as a leader.The turbulence deepened following the conclusion of the match against Railways, when Kunal Singh Rathore, returning from a ban imposed due to a dispute with fellow wicketkeeper-batter Rajkumar Saini, was straightaway instated as the new vice-captain, completely displacing Lomror from the leadership role.Compounding the unrest is the handling of another wicketkeeper-batter, Mukul Choudhary, whose journey through the tournament has been marked by a series of bizarre selection calls.
